name: Venmail SMTP and Lead Finder
author: patacee

sections.description:
Your website sends important emails: customer enquiries, order updates, password resets and more. Venmail SMTP and Lead Finder helps you connect an SMTP provider, check your email setup and find new business opportunities from WordPress.

Send with your preferred SMTP provider. Use Venmail SMTP or another compatible provider for your WordPress emails. Send a test email to an address you control to check your setup.

Check whether your sending IP is blacklisted. Enter the sending IP from a received email and check it against your chosen DNS blocklist. Find reputation issues that may be affecting your email.

Find potential customers. Describe your business or enter a website to discover prospects. You can also search for people at a target company. Create a free Venmail discovery account and verify your email to get started. Account and service limits apply.

See how often your emails are opened. Turn on optional open tracking to see estimated open counts for WordPress HTML emails. Connect a Venmail mailbox to view inbox and sent threads, including estimated open counts for supported sent messages.

Keep track of sending. Optional handoff history records when WordPress hands a message to its configured mailer. Handoff history and open tracking are off by default.

What you need

  • An SMTP provider and its credentials to send email. Venmail is optional for SMTP.
  • A verified Venmail discovery account for customer and company searches. An organization API key is required for name-and-domain prospect lookups.
  • A mailbox-scoped Venmail agent token for inbox and sent messages.
  • Permission to use the chosen DNS blocklist for IP checks.

A discovery account does not include an SMTP mailbox. A test email confirms whether WordPress handed a message to its configured mailer; check the recipient inbox to confirm receipt. A failed or empty blocklist response is inconclusive. Prospect details can be outdated, and email opens are estimates.

The plugin makes no outbound connections or transport changes on activation. Optional handoff history stores status and time for up to 50 entries. Optional first-party open tracking requires HTTPS and stores the subject, time, anonymous token hash and total opens for up to 50 sent messages, without recipient addresses or message bodies. Site owners are responsible for appropriate disclosures and permissions. Both histories can be cleared; no anonymous analytics are collected.

External services

When an administrator requests a prospect lookup, the name and business domain are sent to the Venmail API at https://m.venmail.io. An organization API key is required and the request counts against the account quota. When an administrator requests inbox data, a mailbox-scoped token is sent to the same API. SMTP sends connect to the administrator-configured SMTP provider. Blocklist checks send the reversed IP and chosen zone to the DNS resolver and selected list provider. These services are only used after the administrator configures and requests them.

The requested account setup sends the contact email, business name, optional website, installation ID and generated credential to Venmail. Recovery sends the installation ID and a replacement credential; Venmail emails a verification code to the saved contact address. Discovery requests send the business and targeting details entered by the administrator. When a customer audience is not provided, Venmail may retrieve public website or search information and send it to its AI providers to suggest an audience. Company people searches use public search results. Suggestions and public profile details may be inaccurate. Venmail processes those details under its privacy policy. No account is created until an administrator requests it and confirms the email address.

Administrators may save their own Apify or Brave Search API key from HTTPS WordPress administration. The key is sent to Venmail over HTTPS and stored encrypted by Venmail, not in the WordPress options database. Venmail sends relevant search inputs to the provider with that key. Keys can be removed in the plugin. Queued searches use the key available when they run. Apify lead actor runs request at least 100 results and may trigger additional actor runs. Providers may charge the key owner. Provider availability, quotas and terms apply.

Apify terms: https://docs.apify.com/legal
Apify privacy policy: https://docs.apify.com/legal/privacy-policy
Brave Search API terms: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/terms-of-service
Brave Search API privacy: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/privacy-policy

Venmail terms: https://venmail.io/resources/terms-of-service
Venmail privacy policy: https://venmail.io/resources/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Tools > Venmail email tools.
  3. For SMTP, enter the provider’s settings and credentials, enable SMTP, and save. The initial host is smtp.venmail.io on port 587 with STARTTLS; change it for another provider.
  4. For prospect lookup, save the Venmail organization API key. For inbox access, save an agent token scoped to inbox:read and thread:read.
  5. Send a test to an address you control and check its inbox.
  6. For customer discovery, request a discovery account, verify the emailed code, and save the installation ID for recovery.
sections.faq:
Is a Venmail account required for SMTP?

No. SMTP works with a compatible SMTP provider. Venmail’s prospect and inbox features require the applicable Venmail account and credentials.

Does the test prove delivery?

No. It confirms only whether WordPress handed the message to its configured mailer without reporting an error. Confirm receipt in the recipient inbox.

Where are credentials stored?

SMTP and Venmail credentials are encrypted in the WordPress options database using a key derived from WordPress authentication salts. Anyone with access to both the database and WordPress secrets can decrypt them. Changing salts invalidates stored credentials.

Does the plugin enable open tracking?

Open tracking is off by default. If enabled by an administrator on an HTTPS site, the plugin adds a first-party image to outgoing HTML email. It can also display estimates already reported by Venmail for a connected sent message. A count does not prove that a person read the email.
